text.p: Electronic measurement instrument maker Keithley Instruments Inc on Monday said it sees improved profitability in its 1997 fourth quarter and 1998 fiscal year.

"Our new business initiatives are entering the phase in their commercialization where revenues are beginning to ramp up and the challenge ahead is to manage them profitably," said Joseph Keithley, the company's chairman, president and chief executive, in a statement.
"Overall, we continue to believe strongly that our growth strategy will lead to improved profitability in the fourth quarter and next fiscal year," he added.
He noted that orders for the company's semiconductor products were up from the prior year, and that the he believes that the worst of the semiconductor capital equipment industry slump is behind us.
Earlier, the company reported net income for the third quarter ending June 30 at $0.10 per share, which is the same as last year's third quarter.
